title: Memphis, W. C. Handy, and her first husband Dudley
summary: Austin recalls being in Memphis when Handy wrote St. Louis Blues, and the theater she and Dudley owned.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: And, of course, when they wrote St. Louis Brewers.
When Handley wrote St. Louis Brewers in Memphis, I was there.
Oh, really? You were around at that time?
He worked at White Dixie Park on one side of the fence, and I worked at the Cove Park.
Was that near Beale Street or down in that part? Right on it. Right down there, yes.

He worked over there at the White Park, and he worked over here at the Cove Park. And my house, I was married to Dudley then. I know you've heard of Dudley. Yes, I've heard. I had theatre and... Yes, I've heard the name. Well, that was my first husband. That was your first husband. Yes, and we were brought that theatre there, opened that theatre, bought that theatre. And that's where we separated. And, uh, Klein, the fellow that used to book the shows, whatever, used to book that whole section, he used to come over and he said, Mrs. Dudley, if you ever make up your own mind from Chicago, I want you to write me in the name. I was just thinking about Tommy Ladner.
